threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still take the Overground to get everywhere instead of just walking it. Everyone knows you can’t trip over a local pub or a coffee spot!
Last week on the 35 bus, saw a guy knitting a bright orange scarf while debating the merits of pineapple on pizza with a drunk mate. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling on the street while his dog sat patiently beside him, watching the passersby like a proud parent. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you catch a late-night ski instructor rocking a neon onesie while promoting his pop-up hot chocolate stand. Truly a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they roll their eyes at the tourists snapping pics of the murals while blocking the sidewalk. It's a dance we've mastered.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy arguing with a pigeon over a dropped burrito outside the Muni stop. The bird was surprisingly assertive. Classic Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but miss the hidden art studios in the narrow streets where locals sip coffee and sketch.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them clutching a map, trying to use it while standing in the middle of a busy plaza, completely oblivious to the chaos around them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington. The locals will let you know there's a difference.
Heard a lad on the 3 bus saying he lost his phone trying to impress someone at the Prince Albert—never saw him get off. Brixton nights are wild.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was a local? When a street artist asked me for tips on the best coffee spots—not the other way around.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find graffiti art and flower markets happening side by side on a Tuesday morning, where every corner tells a different story.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they navigate the bus delays—grabbing a taco and rolling their eyes at yet another 14-Mission late arrival.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling flaming torches on the 9 bus while debating the best burrito in the city—only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Sagrada Família is the heart of Barcelona, but Gràcia’s plazas hold the real vibe. It's where the locals unwind and share secrets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their reluctance to try a 'bocata' standing up at the bar. True locals know it's part of the experience.
